questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle marked for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (flammable gases). This also applies to lit cigars, cigarettes, or pipes within 25 feet of vehicles carrying Class 1 (explosives), Class 4 (flammable solids), or Class 4.2 (spontaneously combustible materials).

questions.question: If there is a fire, what should you do before opening trailer doors?

options.text: Check to see if the doors are hot.
Find someone else to open the doors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check to see if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: If your truck is on fire, feel the trailer doors before opening them. Hot doors mean there may be a fire inside the cargo. Keep the doors closed because opening them will give the fire more oxygen and make it worse.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous products are also flammable. Take proper safety steps if you think your cargo might catch fire.

questions.question: When carrying explosives, you may leave your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved parking location for unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: What might tell you that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper works in a business that handles hazardous materials.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The road is made of gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper works in a business that handles hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A clue that a shipment contains hazardous materials is if the shipper works in a business that typically handles them. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control companies, and dealers in explosives or fireworks.

questions.question: You may leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended:

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved parking location for unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material
How quickly the material must reach its destination
The country of origin of the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fall into nine hazard classes. Each class tells you the risks connected to that material.

questions.question: Flammable gases are categorized as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are classified as Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, how can you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.
By keeping the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use electric lights or reflective triangles to warn other drivers. Do not use flares or anything that could spark a fire, since you are carrying flammable materials.

questions.question: When accepting hazardous materials, a driver should check that:

options.text: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping papers are written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages. They must match.

questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not needed for most shipments.
Should be kept in a special compartment in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous material shipments. They tell drivers and workers about the dangers of the cargo.

questions.question: A shipping paper must list:

options.text: The location of fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must list an emergency response telephone number.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves on a compressed gas tank open during loading and unloading. Keep them closed at all other times.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials:

options.text: The hazardous materials must be listed first.
The hazardous materials must be written in larger text.
The hazardous materials must be written in red ink.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazardous materials must be listed first.
questions.explanation: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, list the hazardous materials first.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires to feel them.

questions.explanation: Check each tire before starting a trip. The only way to check tire pressure correctly is to use a tire pressure gauge.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all types of shipping papers.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must appear?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging for the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (for "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, keep liquid discharge valves closed at all times except during loading and unloading.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: basic descriptions and technical names of materials; health hazards; risks of fire or explosion; steps to take in an accident; methods for handling fires; methods for handling spills or leaks; and first aid measures.

questions.question: What is the only way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tire to feel how hard it is.

questions.explanation: Check your tire pressure at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check if your tires have the correct pressure.

questions.question: What is required of someone supervising tank loading?

options.text: Does not need to know what materials are being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified supervisor must watch the loading of hazardous materials. This person must stay within 25 feet of the tank, have a clear view, know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials require a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. The total transport index in one vehicle cannot be more than 50.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must receive training on hazardous materials safety, including how to spot and respond to security threats. Training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: How should you label a small item that is smaller than its label?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and put a paper label on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Mark it with a large orange dot.
Place it in a box with a warning label on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard labels must be on most hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What must you do to complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest?

options.text: Sign it only if you cross into another state.
Sign it only if the weather was hazardous.

questions.explanation: You must sign a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest by hand. The manifest must also include the name and EPA registration number of the shippers, carriers, and destination.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper must package, mark, and label hazardous materials correctly. Drivers should check that materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: What might indicate that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting hazardous cargo.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must describe the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the vehicle will travel less than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must display proper placards before driving. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if it is necessary to protect lives or property in an emergency.
